classification: three-prompt finite operator audit; reconstructed arithmetic matches BNB M=3 and BNB M=1 row calls for every Linear4bit module on captured activations; not a universal numerical proof or speed result
arithmetic_contract_tested: For CUDA FP16 SIMT: round NF4 LUT centroid to FP16; round nested scale to FP16; half2 multiply and round reconstructed weight to FP16; half2 activation-weight product rounded to FP16; convert products to FP32; accumulate pairs serially per lane; warp down-shuffle sum offsets 16,8,4,2,1; add optional FP16 bias in FP32; cast output to FP16 then wrapper dtype.
interpretation: The previously unresolved BNB/Triton linear mismatch was caused by staged FP16 rounding in the BNB SIMT path: both centroid and scale are rounded before their half2 multiply, then activation products are rounded before FP32 accumulation.
The reconstructed operator schedule matched all captured BNB M=3 outputs and all per-row BNB M=1 outputs across 252 modules and three prompts.

This supports B2 quantized-linear operator feasibility for this model revision, BNB version, FP16 compute path, and SM89. It does not establish whole-model exactness for arbitrary inputs, nor prove normalization/attention/KV behavior, nor provide a fast fused implementation.
limits: Three prompts (two HumanEval and one CNN/DailyMail), one forced M=3 block per prompt, one GPU and fixed software/model versions.
Finite captured activations; not a proof for all inputs or all CUDA/compiler/toolchain combinations.
The audit kernel consumes materialized FP16 weights; timings are excluded and this is not the optimized fused kernel.
GSM8K held-out indices 300-349 were not used.
